text: ABSTRACT
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > ABSTRACT

text: It is significantly important to develop novel suppressor to achieve cobalt superconformal filling. Linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV) and impedance spectra (EIS) were coupled together to study the effect of novel dye suppressor nitrotetrazolium blue chloride (NBT) on cobalt electrodeposition. The adsorption behavior of NBT on cobalt substrate was investigated by applying density functional theory (DFT) calculation, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and in situ Raman spectra, while the interaction between NBT and cobalt ions ( Co ^2 +) is analyzed based on topology analysis and interaction region indicator (IRI) analysis. Synergistic suppressing mechanism, namely adsorption effect and coordination effect, was proposed to explain the suppressing effect of NBT during cobalt electrodeposition. The cobalt surface morphology analysis under the influence of NBT demonstrates that NBT is of grain refinement, while XRD analysis indicates that the formation of Co hcp (100) is formed preferentially. The superconformal filling of cobalt is achieved in microvias with different diameters. The cobalt layer is of excellent quality due to low surface deposit thickness (SDT).

text: 1. Introduction
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 1. Introduction

text: With semiconductor technology evolving continuously along the way based on Moore’s Law, the traditional copper damascene process is facing enormous challenges in terms of yield and reliability [1,2]. On one hand, when trench size is decreased to lower than Mean electron free path of copper, the intensified electron scattering at external surfaces and grain boundaries leads to the exponential growth of resistivity of copper interconnect, resulting in severely increased RC delay and IR drop [3,4]. On the other hand, the seed layer and barrier layer increase the proportion of non-conductive material within copper interconnect, further increasing the resistivity [5]. Meanwhile, it is hard to achieve void-defect filling of copper in downscaling interconnect line width since the current density at the opening is increased due to edge effect, which has a negative effect on reliability [6,7]. Among alternative metals, cobalt [8] is regarded as candidate interconnect metal as a result of low line resistivity at advanced node and compatibility to electroplating process compared with Ni [9,10], Ru [11], Au [12], graphene [13,14] etc.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 1. Introduction

text: Electroplating technology is key fabrication process to obtain cobalt interconnect [14]. It is essentially important to introduce proper additives to achieve superconformal growth of cobalt [15,16] since the growth rate at the plane and opening of vias is higher than that in the bottom and sidewalls as a result of mass transfer limitation within vias and edge effect at the opening [17,18]. Several additives used for cobalt superconformal filling has been reported in the literature. Josell et al. investigated branched polyethyleneimine (PEI) as suppressor and proposed S-shaped negative differential resistance (S-NDR) model to predict bottowm-up filling of cobalt [19], while Huang et al. studied the effect of oxime additive and believed that amine groups could coordinate with Co ^2 + to suppress the cobalt electrodeposition [20–22]. He et al. studied the influence of inhibitor polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) on cobalt electrodeposition as well as cobalt superconformal electrodeposition was achieved at trench with high aspect ratio [23].

text: In contrast, Ma et al. proposed adsorption-coordination inhibition mechanism to explain the suppressing effect of malachite green (MG) during cobalt electrodeposition and achieve superconformal filling [24].

text: Although several additives have been investigated, researchers pay little attention to the suppressing mechanism and effective special groups of additives based on experimental analysis and theoretical analysis. Advanced analyzing methods, including in situ Fourier Trans form Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) [25], in situ Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) [26,27] and Scanning Tunneling Microscopy [28], are widely used to study the adsorption behavior of additives. Besides, another emerging method, theoretical calculation is regarded as an effective method for exploiting the suppressing mechanism of additive [29]. For example, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation is widely accepted to analyze the adsorption ability of additive [30,31], while density functional theory (DFT) is often used to predict the effect of additive based on calculated parameters [32] and analyze interaction between metal ions and additive [33,34]. As a result, operando method and theoretical calculation can help researchers better understand the influencing mechanism, which can provide support for future molecule design.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 1. Introduction

text: In this work, a kind of dye molecule Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride (NBT), was used as novel suppressor on cobalt electrodeposition. Electrochemical methods including linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV) and electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) were used together to study the influence of NBT on kinetics of Co ^2 + reduction. Density functional theory (DFT) calculation was accepted to obtain the quantum chemical parameters of NBT. Besides, theoretical calculation, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and in situ Raman spectra were used to study the adsorption of NBT on cobalt substrate. Topology analysis and interaction region indicator (IRI) analysis were accepted to study the coordination between NBT and cobalt ions ( Co ^2 +). The suppressing mechanism of NBT is explained by proposing synergistic suppressing mechanism. The influence of NBT on morphology and crystal orientation is investi gated by SEM and XRD, respectively. Cobalt superconformal growth is achieved at microvias with different diameters.

text: 3.1. Electrochemical study
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.1. Electrochemical study

text: The suppressing effect of NBT on the reduction of Co ^2 + is analyzed by electrochemical method including linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV) and electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS).
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.1. Electrochemical study

text: Fig. 1 (a) shows the effect of NBT on electrochemical reaction. Generally, the increased cathodic polarization indicates that the metal electrodeposition is suppressed. In order to exclude the influence of NBT on hydrogen evolution reaction, LSV curves were measured without the existence of cobalt ions, as shown in Fig. S1. It can be seen that NBT can improve HER at a limited extent. As a result, the strengthened cathodic polarization will reflect the suppressing effect of NBT on cobalt deposition. The cathodic polarization is −1.180 V when NBT concentration is 0 mg/L. After the introduction of NBT, it can be found that even trace NBT can effectively increase the overpotential (more than 35 mV for 5 mg/L). Besides, the cathodic polarization sees an increase from −1.215 V to lower than −1.250 V with NBT increasing from 5 mg/L to 20 mg/L, which illustrates that suppressing effect for the electrodeposition of cobalt is intensified with the increase of NBT concentration and NBT is an effective suppressor for cobalt electrodeposition.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.1. Electrochemical study

text: Electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) are also used to confirm the suppressing effect of NBT on Co ^2 + reduction, as shown in Fig. 1 (b) and Figs. S1 to S3. Generally, the reaction energy barrier increases with impedance ring diameters [40]. As a result, the phenomenon of increasing impedance ring diameters with NBT illustrates that the suppressing effect is intensified by NBT regardless of applied measuring potential, consistent with the analysis from Fig. 1 (a). Besides, the equivalent circuit is established to calculate the charge transfer impedance (Rct) and solution impedance (Rs) by fitting parameters. The calculated results are shown in Fig. 1(c). Rs range from 30.1 to 30.8 Ω, indicating that NBT almost has no influence on solution impedance. The impedance with 5 mg/L is 596.6 Ω, far higher than that of VMS (400.5 Ω), which confirms that trace NBT can lead to strong cathodic polarization. When NBT is higher than 15 mg/L, the increased impedance become larger than 1250 Ω, which is two times higher than VMS, illustrating that NBT is of excellent suppressing effect during cobalt electrodeposition.

text: 3.2. Density functional theory analysis
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.2. Density functional theory analysis

text: The quantum chemical information of molecule is used widely to predict the possible effect [41]. Fig. 2 (a) shows the optimized NBT molecule structure. The benzene and heterocyclic structures connected by carbon chains is regarded to have potential to adsorb on surface compactly. Besides, molecular orbital properties, namely highest occupied molecular orbits (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbits (LUMO), are usually used to analyze the adsorption property of additive [42]. The HOMO and LUMO for NBT are calculated and is shown in Fig.~ 2 ( b) and (c), in which the HOMO and LUMO are mainly distributed on pi electron cloud of benzene and nitrogenous heterocyclic ring, illustrating that adsorption of NBT occurs preferentially on ring structures.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.2. Density functional theory analysis

text: The energy of HOMO and LUMO indicates the electron donating ability and electron accepting ability according to the frontier molecular orbital theory. The relatively low ΔE ( E _LUMO ^- E _HOMO) illustrates that it is easier for the additive molecule to accept and donate electrons at the electrode surface. As a result, there is relationship between the value of ΔE (E LUMO -E HOMO) and the adsorption intensity of additives [43]. Generally, less ΔE means stronger adsorption [44]. E LUMO and E HOMO is - 0.15179 Ha and - 0.26626 Ha, respectively. And the ΔE is 0.11447 Ha, demonstrating that NBT is of potential to adsorb on the cobalt surface during electrodeposition.

text: 3.3. Adsorption analysis
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.3. Adsorption analysis

text: Electrostatic potential (ESP) distribution and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation were applied to study NBT adsorption behavior. Fig.2 (c) shows the ESP distribution histogram and the average potential is 101.15 kcal/mol. Besides, the ESP ranges from 30 kcal/mol to 160 kcal/ mol, indicating that the positively charged NBT is of adsorption potential on cathodic surface due to electrostatic interaction between NBT and cobalt substrate during electrodeposition.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.3. Adsorption analysis

text: Fig. 3 (b) and 3 (c) shows the initial state and the adsorption equi librium state of MD simulation at 298 K with time step of 1 ps and simulation time of 500 ps. It can be seen from cross section image in Fig. 3 (b) that NBT adsorb on the surface with benzene and heterocyclic structures parallel to the substrate, in accordance with prediction of HOMO/LUMO analysis discussed in 3.2. Fig. 3 (c) and 3 (d) show the energy curves and temperature curves. The basically unchanged plots of energy and temperature illustrate that the adsorption equilibrium is achieved. The adsorption energy of NBT is 342.2 kJ/mol, which demonstrates that NBT is of excellent adsorption ability.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.3. Adsorption analysis

text: In order to verify the calculated results, in situ Raman spectra is carried out, as shown in Fig. 4. The typical peaks of NBT appears at 991, 1126, 1186, 1222, 1316, 1364, 1435, 1502, 1597 cm ^- 1, respectively, when cathodic potential changes from open circuit potential (OCP) to - 2.2 V. It can be seen from Table 2 that characteristic peaks appeared at 991 and 1316 cm ^- 1 attribute to stretching vibration of tetrazole ring N-N[4 5, 4 6 ], while 1222 cm ^- 1 and 1364 cm ^- 1 are due to tetrazole ring N-N bending vibration and -tetrazole bending vibration [47,48]. The characteristic peaks of 1126 cm ^- 1 and 1186~cm^-1 is aromatic C-H bending vibration [49,50] as well as 1435 cm ^- 1 is aromatic C-H stretching vibration [51]. In contrast, C–N stretching vibration and NO _2 stretching vibration appear at 1 5 0 2 ~ cm ^- 1 and 1597 cm ^- 1 separately [ 4 8, 5 1 ]. Overall, the theoretical calculation analysis and in situ Raman spectra analysis illustrate that NBT can absorb well on cobalt surface to reduce active sites and suppress the cobalt electrodeposition.

text: 3.4. Coordination analysis
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.4. Coordination analysis

text: During the electrodeposition, the nitrogenous heterocyclic ring of the adsorbed NBT will accept electrons from cathodic surface due to the local minima appear at nitrogenous heterocyclic ring, as shown in Fig. 5 (a), and later the nitrogenous heterocyclic ring is opened [52,53]. When cobalt ions move toward the cathode surface, a possible coordination interaction would be formed between cobalt ions and opened nitrogenous heterocyclic ring.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.4. Coordination analysis

text: Topology analysis based on atoms in molecules (AIM) theory was carried out to study the potential interaction [54] and the calculated results were shown in Fig.~ 5 ( b) and relevant properties of bond critical point (BCP) were summarized in Table 3. The electron density ( ρ _ BCP) and Laplacian of electron density ( \bigtriangledown ^ 2 ρ _ BCP) are used widely to judge the bond property. The bond properties among N1, N2 and cobalt ions are similar to that among N 3, N4 and cobalt ions, indicating symmetry of NBT. The ρ _ BCP and \bigtriangledown ^ 2 ρ _ BCP formed between N1 and cobalt ions are 0.0827 a.u. and 0.6225 a.u., indicating that the interaction between N1 and cobalt ion is of ionic bond property since ρ _ BCP is lower than 0.1 a.u. and \bigtriangledown ^ 2 ρ _ BCP is positive. Likewise, the interaction between N2 and cobalt ions is also within the criterion for ionic bonding interaction. Besides, the energy density ( H _ BCP) and potential energy density ( V r _ BCP) at bond critical point are used to compare the bond strength.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.4. Coordination analysis

text: It can be seen that the values formed between N1 and cobalt ions are larger than that formed between N2 and cobalt ions, indicating that the interaction between N1 and cobalt ions is stronger.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.4. Coordination analysis

text: Similar conclusion can be found in Fig. 5 (b) since the bond length (1.96 Å) between N1 and cobalt ion is lower than that between N2 and cobalt ions ( 1.9 7 A). The strong coordination between NBT and cobalt ions can effectively increase the energy barrier when cobalt ions are reduced to cobalt layer.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.4. Coordination analysis

text: The visualization of coordination interaction in NBT - Co ^ 2 + complexes was drawn according to IRI analysis [37], in which the sign(λ 2) ρ function can be drawn as isosurfaces to show the bonding region more directly and intuitively. ρ represents the electron density and the sign ( λ _ 2) is the second largest eigenvalue of Hessian of ρ _ ρ. As shown in Fig. 5 (c), the blue region indicates the interatomic interaction. It can be seen clearly that the interatomic interaction exists between Co ^ 2 + and NBT, illustrating that NBT can coordinate with Co ^ 2 +. Fig. 5 (d) shows the 2D color-filled plane IRI map. Obviously, the interaction region between Co ^ 2 + and NBT can be observed. As a result, it can be concluded that there is strong coordination interaction between Co ^ 2 + and NBT.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.4. Coordination analysis

text: In summary, synergistic suppressing mechanism was proposed to illustrate the excellent suppressing ability of NBT during cobalt electrodeposition. On one hand, NBT is of excellent adsorption ability on cathodic surface since it is positively charged and is full of p i electron cloud of benzene and nitrogenous heterocyclic ring, which can reduce the active sites for reduction of Co ^2 + (Adsorption effect). On the other hand, the nitrogenous heterocyclic ring opening due to accepting electrons from cathodic surface leads to that NBT can coordinate with Co ^2 + when Co ^2 + go through the NBT adsorption layer, which further increase the energy barrier (Coordination effect).

text: 3.5. Effect of NBT on morphology
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.5. Effect of NBT on morphology

text: The effect of NBT on cobalt layer morphology was studied by SEM, as shown in Fig. 6. The inserted figure shows the grain size distribution and mean grain size. The cobalt layer is relatively compact when NBT ranges from 0 mg/L to 15 mg/L. However, it should be noted that the cobalt layer is full of large and coarse grains (mean grain size of about 416 nm) without NBT. The quality of cobalt layer can be effectively improved by introducing NBT, as shown in Fig. 6 (b) to (d). The cobalt layer becomes more uniform when NBT concentration rises from 5 mg/L to 15 mg/L, indicating that NBT can improve the surface morphology. Besides, the grain size is about 356 nm when NBT concentration is 5 mg/L. In contrast, the grain size is reduced to about 264 nm and lower than 240 nm when NBT concentration is 10 mg/L and 15 mg/L, respectively. The phenomenon of decreased grain size with rising of NBT concentration indicates that NBT is of grain refinement and the improved surface smoothness is conducive to lowering the losses of signal transmission.

text: 3.7. Electroplating
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.7. Electroplating

text: The superconformal growth of cobalt within microvias is achieved to confirm the effect of NBT, as shown in Fig. 8. The current transients are provided in supplementary (Fig. S5) and the current density is about 1.6 mA/cm2 while calculated current efficiency is 40 %. Fig. 8 (a) shows the shape evolution in microvias of 150 μm during cobalt electrodeposition. The cobalt electrodeposition at the opening of microvias is effectively suppressed due to fast mass transfer of NBT near the plane and opening. In contrast, the supplementary rate of NBT at the bottom is lowered than consuming rate as a result of relatively slow mass transfer of NBT from bulk solution into microvias. Cobalt layer began to grow from the bottom to the top of the microvias, as shown in a2 (8h) in Fig. 8 (a). After being electrodeposited for 16 h, cobalt layer grows near the opening of microvias while the surface deposit thickness (SDT) is lowered than 16 μm, indicating that NBT is of excellent selectivity.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.7. Electroplating

text: Likewise, the superconformal electrodeposition of cobalt is achieved at microvias with 100 μm and 50 μm, as shown in Fig. 8 (b) and (c). The electrodeposition time for b2 and b3 in microvias of 100 μm is 6 h and 12 h, while the electroplating time for c2 and c3 in 50 μm is 4 h and 8 h. The SDT values obtained in 100 μm and 50 μm are 8.8 μm and 4.9 μm, respectively. Overall, NBT is of excellent performance to achieve cobalt superconformal growth.
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 3.7. Electroplating

text: In order to further illustrate the influence of NBT on cobalt growth within microvias, schematic diagram is shown in Fig. 9. At the initial stage (a), NBT is distributed uniformly on plating solution and the growth rate is the same. After that, due to continuously consummation in microvias, the concentration gradient of NBT is gradually formed since the supply rate of NBT provided by mass transfer from bulk solution into microvias is lower than the consuming rate, leading to that the growth rate within microvias is higher than plane and opening. Cobalt layer begin to grow from bottom to top, as is shown in stage b and stage c. Finally, cobalt superconformal growth is achieved.

text: 4. Conclusion
section: Investigation of novel suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride on cobalt superconformal growth > 4. Conclusion

text: The suppressing effect of dye molecule Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride (NBT) on cobalt electrodeposition is investigated by LSV and EIS. DFT calculation and MD simulation is used to study the suppressing mechanism. Quantum chemical calculation, MD simulation and in situ Raman spectra confirms the strong adsorption effect of NBT on cobalt substrate. Besides, topology analysis and IRI analysis were applied to study the coordination effect between NBT and Co ^2 +. Synergistic sup pressing mechanism (adsorption effect and coordination effect) is proposed to demonstrate the influence of NBT. The effect of NBT on morphology of cobalt layer is studied and NBT is of grain refinement. What’s more, the introduction of NBT is conducive for the formation of Co (1 0 0) and can suppress the Co (1 1 0) crystal plane. Superconformal electrodeposition is achieved at micovias with different diameters. The relatively low SDT values (15.9 μm for 150 μm, 8.8 μm for 100 μm and 4.9 μm for 50 μm) indicates that NBT is of excellent selectivity.
